lesson.topicTitle: 1. Structure, Bonding & Introduction to Organic Chemistry

specAnchors.text: be able to use chemical equations to calculate reacting masses and vice versa, using the concepts of amount of substance and molar mass

primer.text: A balanced equation is a mole contract between reactants and products. This note runs masses across that contract - divide by molar mass, apply the coefficient ratio, multiply back out - and reverses the whole chain to reconstruct an unknown equation from nothing but experimental masses.

modules.title: Mass through the mole bridge
modules.opening: A balanced equation is a mole contract, and masses must enter it through the mole bridge. This lesson runs the standard five-step chain - equation, Mr values, moles, ratio, mass back out - on magnesium burning to magnesium oxide.
keyPoints: Convert the given mass to moles with n = m / Mr before touching the equation.
The balanced equation's coefficients give the mole ratio between the substances.
Convert the answer moles back to mass with m = n x Mr.
7.5 g of magnesium (0.3086 mol) gives 0.3086 mol MgO, which is 12.4 g.

low.restatement: Grams go in, moles cross the ratio, grams come out: divide, scale, multiply.
low.analogy: The mole is the customs office between mass country and ratio country - nothing crosses without declaring its moles.
low.examPointer: Write the balanced equation first; the ratio marks follow from it, and examiners award them line by line.

medium.restatement: Because coefficients count formula units, masses only acquire meaning after conversion to moles; the ratio then rescales the moles, and the product's Mr converts back to grams.
medium.analogy: It is a currency exchange with a fixed exchange rate: pounds to moles, apply the contract's rate, moles back to pounds.
medium.examPointer: Any mass unit works - grams or tonnes - as long as both sides use it consistently; the proportionality is unit-agnostic.

modules.title: Balancing backwards from masses
modules.opening: Experimental masses can reconstruct an unknown equation. This lesson reverses the chain: masses to moles, moles to the smallest-integer ratio, ratio to coefficients - using carbon reducing zinc oxide to metallic zinc.
keyPoints: Known masses of every substance convert to moles with n = m / Mr.
Dividing all mole values by the smallest gives the coefficient set.
1.2 g carbon with 16.2 g zinc oxide yields 0.1 : 0.2, so C + 2ZnO -> 2Zn + CO2.
The molar ratio from a balanced equation is the ratio of amounts reacting, not of masses.

low.restatement: Turn each measured mass into moles, divide by the smallest, and the whole numbers become the coefficients.
low.analogy: It is the empirical-formula routine wearing an equation's clothes: same divide-by-smallest trick, different destination.
low.examPointer: Check conservation: the coefficients you derive must leave atom counts equal on both sides.

medium.restatement: Because moles count formula units, the mole quotients ARE the relative formula-unit counts; simplifying them to integers recovers the smallest equation that reproduces the experiment.
medium.analogy: Like reconstructing a recipe from what the kitchen scale read: weigh each ingredient, divide by portion size, and the recipe ratios fall out.
medium.examPointer: State the ratio step explicitly (divide by 0.1 here); skipping it looks like the coefficients were guessed.

glossary.definition: The fixed proportion of amounts, in moles, fixed by a balanced equation's coefficients.
The maximum product mass predicted by a reacting-mass calculation, before real-world losses.
The mole-bookkeeping that connects amounts of reactants and products through a balanced equation's coefficients.

workedExample.prompt: 7.5 g of magnesium burns completely in oxygen. Calculate the maximum mass of magnesium oxide formed. (Ar: Mg 24.3, O 16.0)
workedExample.finalAnswer: 12.4 g of magnesium oxide - the theoretical yield from 7.5 g of magnesium.
